pll2d14c4-d1e3519.summary: Answers the worry how naturally flowing waters stand above heaven: God binds waters in clouds (Job 26:8) and can suspend waters above the heavenly sphere, solid like ice; what they are and why made, their maker knows.
claims: God can suspend waters above heaven.

pll2d14c4-d1e3540.summary: Concludes that it has been shown which heaven was made (that of the stars, above the air), from what matter (waters), and what kind of waters are above it (solidified like ice).
claims: The firmament is the starry heaven made from water, with ice-like waters above.

pll2d14c4-d1e3543.summary: Reports others who say the heaven above the air is of fiery nature, pure fire above the air, from which the stars and luminaries were made; Augustine seems to agree.
claims: Some hold the upper heaven is fiery.

pll2d14c4-d1e3550.summary: Notes Augustine asks without solving whether 'firmament' means the heaven beyond the air or the air itself, preferring the former; he says the waters above are drawn up as vapor in very light drops, as the cloudy air draws up water vapor and later rains it down; so why not believe finer vapors above the lighter heaven?
claims: Augustine leaves the firmament's identity open.
The upper waters may exist as fine vapor.

pl-l2d14c4.summary: Answers how waters, naturally flowing downward, can stand above heaven: God, who binds waters in clouds (Job 26:8), can suspend them above the sphere solidified like ice; their nature and purpose are known to their maker. Some think the heaven above the air is of fiery nature, from which stars were made, which Augustine seems to accept. Augustine asks without resolving whether 'firmament' means the heaven above the air or the air itself, preferring the former, and suggests the upper waters are drawn up in fine vapors, as air holds water vapor.
claims: God can suspend waters above the heavens.
The upper waters may be solidified like ice, or held as fine vapor.
Some hold the heaven above the air is fiery, the source of the stars.
Augustine leaves open whether the firmament is the heaven above the air or the air.
